nodes.summary: For every base $d$, every modulus $q > 0$, all lists of natural numbers $P$ (the pattern) and $T$ (the text) and every natural number $s$, Rabin–Karp matching of $P$ in $T$ with base $d$ and modulus $q$ reports the offset $s$ if and only if $P$ matches $T$ at $s$, that is, $s \le |T|$ and $P$ is a prefix of the suffix of $T$ that starts at position $s$ (counting from $0$).
nodes.title: Correctness of Rabin–Karp matching

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a base, $q > 0$ a modulus, $a$ a natural number and $m$, $n$ natural numbers with $0 < m \le n$. Let $C$ be the counted cost of Rabin–Karp matching with base $d$ and modulus $q$ of the pattern $a^m$ in the text $a^n$ (the lists of $m$ and of $n$ copies of $a$), minus $8m - 1$, with subtraction truncated at $0$. Then $m(n - m + 1) \le C \le 10\,m(n - m + 1)$.
nodes.title: Matching cost of Rabin–Karp on repeated-symbol words

nodes.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and list of natural numbers $T$, Rabin–Karp matching of the empty pattern in $T$ returns the list $[0, 1, \dots, |T|]$ of all offsets from $0$ to $|T|$ in increasing order, at counted cost $0$.
nodes.title: Rabin–Karp matching with the empty pattern

nodes.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and lists of natural numbers $P$ and $T$ with $|T| < |P|$, Rabin–Karp matching of $P$ in $T$ returns no offsets, at counted cost exactly $1 + 2(|P| - 1) + 6|T|$.
nodes.title: Rabin–Karp matching with a pattern longer than the text

nodes.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and lists of natural numbers $P$ and $T$, the offsets returned by Rabin–Karp matching of $P$ in $T$ form a strictly increasing list; in particular no offset is reported twice.
nodes.title: Rabin–Karp reports offsets in increasing order

nodes.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$ and lists of natural numbers $P$ and $T$, the list of offsets returned by Rabin–Karp matching of $P$ in $T$ with base $d$ and modulus $q$ equals the list returned by naive matching of $P$ in $T$.
nodes.title: Rabin–Karp and naive matching return the same offsets

nodes.summary: For every base $d$, modulus $q > 0$, symbol $a \in \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $m \le n$, Rabin–Karp matching of the pattern $a^m$ in the text $a^n$ (the lists of $m$ and of $n$ copies of $a$) returns $[0, 1, \dots, n - m]$, that is, every shift in increasing order, including overlapping ones.

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
